symptom: `diag loop-report` reported the app-restart bill as a floor built from the minority of boots that closed: on two measured projects 4 of 30 and 7 of 34 `run` invocations were counted, so `run` read as 27-29% of mxcli's wall time when multiplying the boot count by the per-boot median gave ~35 and ~50 minutes against sessions of 5 h and 2 h 45. The proposal's words: "a boot that is killed never writes a summary record, so its duration is not counted at all". The restart is the largest wall-time item in an agent session and it was the one the instrument could not see (PROPOSAL_agent_loop_efficiency.md item 2d).
cause: THREE independent reasons a run left no session_end, and fixing only the obvious one changes nothing for `run`. (1) main() exited through os.Exit(1) on the Execute error path, so a command that merely RETURNED an error wrote no summary and lost its duration. (2) Each command does `defer logger.Close()` after newLoggedExecutor, and that defer runs while the command is RETURNING - before cobra hands the error back - so under diaglog's first-wins rule the command always closed the session and recorded it as clean, making main's close a no-op. (3) `run --local` is a `Run:` command (not RunE) that calls os.Exit at every failure site, including its normal 'the runtime stopped' ending; 258 os.Exit sites in cmd/mxcli and 78 `Run:` commands cannot return an error at all, so no close-on-error can reach them, and a SIGKILLed boot writes nothing either way.
file: mdl/diaglog/diaglog.go (HeartbeatInterval, startHeartbeat, closeWithExit, Close now a no-op for the process session), cmd/mxcli/main.go (runCLI closes on both paths), cmd/mxcli/diag_loop_report.go (session_alive paired by pid -> invocation.Floor, verbStats.FloorSec/UnmeasuredSec, loopReport.UnclosedFloorSeconds/UnmeasuredSeconds/ExitedNonZero); tests cmd/mxcli/diag_loop_report_test.go, cmd/mxcli/main_session_close_test.go, mdl/diaglog/{diaglog,singleton}_test.go
insight: **A periodic heartbeat is the only fix that reaches every death mode, and it needs cooperation from none of them.** The instinct - make the failure path close the session - was measured as insufficient in one command: `mxcli check /nonexistent.mdl` writes no session_end even after the fix, because it exits inside the command, and `run` does the same at every site. One `session_alive` line every 30s bounds a killed run from below for SIGKILL, os.Exit and a crash alike, without touching 258 call sites. **The real run is what refuted my own first fix**: the log showed a failing `check` closing with exit_code 0, which located the defer-ordering bug (2) that no unit test would have shown, because the singleton cannot be reopened inside one test binary. **Keep a measurement and an extrapolation in separate fields.** wall_seconds stays the closed runs only; unclosed_floor_seconds is measured from heartbeats; unmeasured_estimate_seconds extrapolates ONLY the unclosed runs that left no heartbeat, at their verb's median, and reports 0 rather than a guess when no run of that verb closed - the ako/mxcli#620 lesson, where one field counting two populations is how a report starts lying. Double-counting is the trap: a run with a floor must not also be estimated. **Two existing tests encoded the old contract and had to change** (TestCloseWritesOneSessionEnd asserted a command's Close writes the record - its own comment already said the first close must not end the session while the command runs, so the test pinned the bug it described). Controls: stubbing the estimate reproduces '26 unclosed runs, 0 visible seconds'; removing main's close fails the call-site guard; dropping the exit_code attr fails the diaglog test; pairing heartbeats positionally credits a child's liveness to its parent. End to end on a real log with a real SIGKILL, a 40s process: pre-change binary '0.0s across the runs that closed, UNCLOSED 1'; after, 'Unclosed, at least: 30.0s' and +FLOOR 30.0s on the row.
